senses.gloss: (b. h.) pr. n. pl. Sodom, one of the cities in the plain of Jordan destroyed for their wickedness.
units: Snh. X, 3 (108ᵃ) (ref. to Ps. I, 5) אלו אנשי ס׳ this alludes to the men of S. Ib. 109ᵇ ארבעה … בס׳ וכ׳ four judges lived in S. &c., v. זְיָיפִי; a. fr.—מִדַּת ס׳ Sodomitic rule, unfairness, selfishness.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 5:10">Ab. V, 10</cite> ‘mine is mine, and thine is thine’, <he>זו היא מ׳ ס׳</he> that is a Sodomitic principle (justice without charity).
<cite ref="Bava Batra 12b:14">B. Bath. 12ᵇ</cite> <he>כופין על מ׳ ס׳</he> the law may use force against unfairness (where one claims a privilege which causes the neighbor no loss); a. fr.—
Ib. 114ᵇ הלכתא … יוסף בס׳ Ar. (ed. בשדה) the law follows R. Joseph’s opinion as to using force against unfairness.—ימא דס׳ the Lake of Sodom (usu. ימא דמילחא).
<cite ref="Shabbat 108b:9">Sabb. 108ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="I00076"><he>טְבַע</he> I</cite>; a. e.
